This allows us to define a model-independent distance to integrability. We show that standard measures of chaos interpolate between integrable and chaotic values with increasing values of this distance. However, there is a large variation across models and the distance to integrability provides additional information not directly provided by these diagnostics.

title: Exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
comment: 29 pages, submission includes zip file with ancillary material
summary: The static interaction potential of two non-spinning point masses in general relativity was previously computed through seventh post-Newtonian order using methods of effective field theory. Its probe limit, or zeroth-self-force contribution, is determined exactly by the Schwarzschild geometry. We derive a closed-form expression for the static first-self-force correction, quadratic in the light mass, and establish its weak-field expansion to all orders. Working in harmonic gauge, we construct the required Green function for the coupled linearised gravitational equations about the Schwarzschild background. We fix its homogeneous contributions and regularised coincident limit by matching to the dimensionally continued point-source theory. The result reproduces known perturbative coefficients and determines all higher static post-Newtonian coefficients in this mass sector.

title: Quantized valley source in bilayer graphene via adiabatic quantum pumping
summary: We propose a quantized valley source based on adiabatic quantum pumping in bilayer graphene in the presence of both quantum spin Hall and quantum valley Hall effects. By periodically modulating the gate voltages of two quantum dots coupled to a bilayer graphene nanoribbon, the helical edge states enable the generation of a pure valley current. Depending on the geometry of quantum dots, the number of emitted valley pairs either forms quantized plateaus or varies continuously with the pumping amplitude. The quantized plateau structure can be tuned by the static gate voltage and by the coupling between the quantum dots and the ribbon. Quantized valley pairs are robust against Anderson disorder applied in the quantum dots and persist for both zigzag and armchair quantum-dot boundaries. These results demonstrate that adiabatic quantum pumping provides a route toward electrically controllable quantized valley sources.

title: A Koszul-Type Splitting Theorem for Complex Supermanifolds
summary:
We study the splitting problem for complex supermanifolds using formal exponential maps and Ehresmann connections. We show that every formal exponential map induces a splitting of the underlying supermanifold. Furthermore, we establish that every Ehresmann connection determines a linearization of the infinite jet space, extending the corresponding construction for ordinary manifolds to supermanifolds.
  For Ehresmann connections preserving the zero section, we construct a formal exponential map in two ways: via the linearization of the infinite jet space and directly from the connection operator. We prove that both constructions yield the same map and induce the same splitting, thereby generalizing Koszul's splitting theorem from linear connections to zero-section-preserving Ehresmann connections. Finally, we provide examples showing that, without this assumption, the two constructions may yield different splittings, or one or both of them may fail to induce a splitting.

title: Surrogate model of gravitational waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries based on the hybridization of WaSABI-C inspirals with numerical relativity waveforms
summary: With the incorporation of aligned-spin dynamics into self-force waveform models, such as the WaSABI-C inspiral model, and with the release of the SXS collaboration's third public catalog of NR simulations, the gravitational waveform modeling community has made significant advances in the modeling of spinning, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries. In light of these developments, we present WaSABINRHybSur2dq15, the first surrogate model to incorporate information from self-force theory, post-Newtonian theory, and numerical relativity. The model is trained on 65 hybrid waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries with mass ratios spanning 1:1.25 to 1:20 and aligned-spins for the primary black hole ranging -0.5 to 0.5. The hybrid waveforms are generated from a set of WaSABI-C inspirals and NR waveforms from the third SXS public catalog. The model covers the parameter domain $1.25 \leq q \leq 15$ and $|χ_{1z}| \leq 0.5$, and includes the $(2,2),\, (2,1),\, (3,3),\, (4,4),$ and $(5,5)$ spin-weighted spherical harmonic modes. The model also spans the entire LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) frequency band (with $f_{\text{low}}=20$ Hz) for total masses $M \gtrsim 111.5\,M_{\odot}$. We find that the WaSABINRHybSur2dq15 model faithfully reproduces the hybrid waveforms with mismatches less than $10^{-3}$ for total masses in the range $80\,M_{\odot} \leq M \leq 300\,M_{\odot}$.

title: Topological Multi-Natural Inflation
summary: We investigate topological inflation in minimal multi-natural inflation, in which the axion potential consists of two cosine terms. Focusing on the high-scale regime, we perform a systematic parameter scan for representative ratios of the two periods and identify regions consistent with current constraints on the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The interplay of the two harmonics allows departures from the quartic hilltop limit and accommodates the higher spectral index favored by recent cosmological data combinations. We characterize the hilltop and near-inflection-point branches and analyze the associated vacuum structure and domain-wall properties. We also discuss a symmetry-breaking origin of the required domain walls when the inflaton is the angular component of a complex scalar field. We identify regions in which the observational constraints and the adopted criteria for topological inflation are simultaneously satisfied, including regions with a sub-Planckian axion decay constant. Our results show that the observational tension encountered in the minimal quartic double-well model need not extend to topological inflation in a minimal multi-natural axion potential.

title: Beyond Synthesis Conditions: Linking In-situ Growth Dynamics to Carbon Nanotube Forest Properties through Multimodal Machine Learning
summary: Machine learning for chemical vapor deposition (CVD) of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) has largely mapped static synthesis conditions to final properties, implicitly treating these conditions as a complete description of growth. Here, we test this assumption by integrating gas-flow conditions with in-situ time-resolve growth profiles (growth curves) of vertically aligned CNT forests. We introduce an observation-window analysis, in which prediction is evaluated as a function of observation time by providing models with the growth curve only up to progressively later times, to determine not only whether a property can be predicted, but when the necessary information becomes available during synthesis. Clustering of normalized growth curves revealed distinct growth patterns independent of final forest height. The gas conditions alone could predict the initial growth rate but not the growth lifetime and failed to capture the variation in yield (R^2<0). Adding the growth curve improved yield prediction (R^2~0.4-0.5), with the relevant information emerging during the intermediate and later stages of growth rather than at its onset. In contrast, density and G/D ratio, which forest height does not record, showed no consistent improvement. The maximum height and lifetime could be estimated with moderate accuracy midway through the 10-min growth. Permutation feature importance identified water vapor and H_2, both linked to catalyst activity, as the most informative gas variables. These results indicate that variation unexplained by synthesis conditions is not merely noise but reflects an evolving catalyst state, and they establish mid-growth decision points for autonomous synthesis, enabling early termination of unpromising batches and, ultimately, in-batch adjustment of growth conditions.

title: Oscillatory instability of subcritical stationary solutions in the parametrically driven, damped nonlinear Dirac equation
summary:
The dynamics of the nonlinear Dirac equation (NLDE) under the influence of dissipation and parametric forcing exhibit complex phenomenologies, including soliton destruction and chaotic transitions, which have been extensively observed in numerical simulations. However, a rigorous analytical understanding of the underlying instability mechanisms in the subcritical regime has remained open.
  In this work, we provide a theoretical answer to these numerical findings by establishing the spectral instability of the fundamental soliton solution. Our methodology relies on a three-step approach linking local asymptotic analyses with global topological arguments. First, we characterize the generalized null space at the critical parameter ($λ_c$), revealing the onset of instability through the splitting of the zero eigenvalue within a parity-dependent subspace. Second, in the non-relativistic limit ($λ\to 0$), we use a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction to reduce the linearized Dirac's operators into a Pöschl--Teller Schrödinger operator, thereby identifying the instability source as a unique real pair of discrete eigenvalues in the restricted problem. Third, we extend these local results to the entire subcritical domain using a topological continuation argument, which tracks the invariance of the spectral parity in a subset of the complex plane. These analytical results rigorously confirm the instability of the soliton, providing the mathematical mechanism for the wave collapse observed in the driven-damped system.

title: Tracing source imprints on the gravitational direct wave
comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, plus Supplemental Material. To be submitted to Physical Review D Letters
summary: The direct wave component of black hole (BH) ringdown, revealed through quasinormal-mode filters, carries a non-quasinormal-mode imprint of the plunging perturber's dynamics. However, the connection between the source trajectory and the observed direct wave remains incompletely understood. We first show that the full waveform filtered by the frequency-dependent black hole response gives a substantially more localized kernel than the standard rational filter approach. We then show that analytically continuing the Teukolsky source variables to complex coordinates allows for a semianalytic direct wave which closely reproduces numerical integration throughout the entire plunge. Our generalized steepest-descent method clarifies how coherent emission shapes the imprint of source dynamics on the observed direct wave beyond the light-cone picture.

title: The Standard Model with Non-Anticommuting $γ_5$ in the BMHV Scheme
summary: The Breitenlohner-Maison/'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme provides a treatment of $γ_5$ in dimensional regularisation (DReg) that is guaranteed to be self-consistent at all orders, but it breaks gauge and BRST invariance at the regularised level, which must be restored by suitable counterterms. We present the complete 1-loop renormalisation of the full Standard Model in the BMHV scheme in general $R_ξ$-gauge, including all singular and all finite symmetry-restoring counterterms. We further analyse the impact of evanescent gauge interactions, which allow the photon and gluon currents to be treated either 4- or $D$-dimensionally. We show that QCD always contributes to the symmetry breaking, so that the Standard Model must be treated as a whole, and we recommend a purely 4-dimensional treatment of electroweak gauge interactions. Our results provide a necessary step towards multi-loop electroweak precision calculations with a fully consistent treatment of $γ_5$.

title: Informative Fisher Modes in Neural Networks as a Result of Explicit Symmetry Breaking
summary: Learning in a neural network takes place on a high dimensional, non-convex loss landscape, the Hessian curvature of which dictates the learning dynamics. Despite its high dimensionality, the large number of architectural symmetries explains some of the geometric of this landscape, in particular flat directions, i.e. near-zero modes of the Hessian. These architectural symmetries have therefore been suggested as an organizing principle of deep learning. It remains an open question, though, wether there are additional organizing principles in the remaining degrees of freedom in the learning dynamic. Here we identify task-dependent contingent symmetries as such an additional organizing principle. We show that non-flat learning directions emerge due to explicit breaking of these contingent symmetries. We isolate this symmetry in an analytically solvable minimal model. Furthermore, we show that, by tuning an L2 penalty, signatures of the symmetry breaking become measurable. As a consequence of the same mechanism, adding noise to the data drives the model through a sequence of broken symmetry recoveries in the form of Baik-Ben-Arous-Péché (BBP) transitions. We demonstrate analytically for linear and numerically for deep linear networks that the contingent symmetry group remains explicit, and that the symmetry-breaking mechanism identifies which Hessian modes carry task-specific information. These signatures are measurable without a symmetry-group description and, hence, offer a route to study symmetry breaking as a more general principle in nonlinear networks and other learning systems.

title: On the properties of the potential and the spherical harmonic expansions for general planets
summary:
The convergence of spherical harmonic expansions (SHEs) of gravitational potentials below the Brillouin sphere has been a long-standing problem in potential theory and geodesy. In previous work, some of the present authors gave a necessary and sufficient condition for convergence along a fixed ray, formulated in terms of analyticity of a longitudinal average of the balayage density. In the present paper, we extend these results to arbitrary physical solid planets, assuming only that the planet is a compact subset of $\mathbb R^3$ and that its density belongs to $L^\infty$. We establish sharp regularity properties of the gravitational potential at the Brillouin sphere. The potential and its first derivative extend continuously to the sphere, the first derivative is locally Hölder continuous with exponent $1/2$, and the second derivative satisfies the optimal bound $V''(z)=O\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial\mathbb D)^{-1/2}\bigr)$ under nontangential approach from the exterior.
  We also obtain sharp estimates for the spherical harmonic coefficients: $a_\ell=O(\ell^{-3/2}).$ If, for almost every latitude, the Brillouin sphere is a one-sided Lebesgue point from the interior of the longitudinally averaged density, then $a_\ell=o(\ell^{-3/2}).$ Both estimates are optimal. We explicitly recover the balayage density on the Brillouin sphere from the exterior gravitational potential, and its circular averages from the potential along a single radial line. Finally, we give a physical characterization of convergence of the SHE below the Brillouin sphere. If the SHE converges at such a point, then, after truncating the planet at any suitable intermediate radius, the gravitational potential of the removed outer part is completely determined by that of the remaining truncated planet. This provides a direct interpretation of the strong constraint imposed by convergence below the Brillouin sphere.

title: Interacting scalar-fermion two-component dark matter in a gauged $\boldsymbol{U(1)_{B-L}}$ model
summary: We propose an interacting two-component dark matter model based on a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model, which also accommodates neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism. The dark sector consists of a Dirac fermion $χ$ and a complex scalar $S$, which can both be stable without imposing an additional discrete symmetry and are directly coupled by a gauge-invariant Yukawa interaction. The resulting conversion, semi-conversion, and semi-annihilation processes lead to a genuinely coupled freeze-out. After imposing collider and dark matter constraints, we identify viable solutions away from the $Z'$ resonance for both mass hierarchies, $m_S > m_χ$ and $m_S < m_χ$. Despite the strong direct-detection constraints, part of the surviving parameter space remains within the reach of next-generation experiments.

title: IRIS: an agentic eye on symmetry-derived paths and energy landscapes of structural phase transitions
summary: Structural phase transitions underpin ferroelectric and multiferroic functionality, but constructing interpretable energy landscapes remains dependent on specialist expertise. Predicting this behaviour rests on Landau free energies expanded in symmetry-adapted order parameters: their coefficients classify a transition, expose the couplings between distortions, set switching paths and barriers, and parametrize phase-field and effective-Hamiltonian models at larger scales. Obtaining these coefficients from first principles means sampling the Born--Oppenheimer energy surface along symmetry-derived structural paths, which requires crystallographic analysis, reliable structure generation and extensive computation, especially for coupled multidimensional order parameters. Here we introduce IRIS, an agentic workflow that converts plain-language requests and crystal structures into symmetry-adapted energy landscapes and fitted Landau energy models. Deterministic gates govern acceptance of structures, calculations and fits, while language models interpret requests and select constrained recovery actions. Applications across six compounds include a six-dimensional BiFeO$_3$ landscape that separates competition between polar and tilt amplitudes from directional locking and ranks homogeneous switching pathways. Controlled replays detected all 53 injected faults; disabling gates allowed 14 silent errors. Four prospective BaTiO$_3$ runs produced fitted landscapes from 96 density-functional calculations in 34 minutes total without intervening human decisions. IRIS makes physical model construction a reusable computational capability and provides a framework for scientific automation grounded in explicit verification.

title: Metastability of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional Ginzburg--Landau model with pinning
summary: We study the persistence of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional magnetic Ginzburg--Landau model with a spatially dependent pinning term. Factoring out the equilibrium profile associated with the pinning term reduces the problem to the analysis of a weighted Ginzburg--Landau functional. In the extreme type-II regime, we construct locally minimizing vortexless configurations for applied fields extending far beyond the first critical field. We obtain quantitative estimates showing that these configurations remain close, up to gauge transformations, to a Meissner-type state determined by a weighted London problem. We also prove the uniqueness, up to gauge transformations, of the locally minimizing Meissner-type branch within a quantitatively controlled class of local minimizers. A central difficulty is to derive elliptic estimates that remain uniform in the Ginzburg--Landau parameter in the presence of the resulting spatially dependent weight. Under a small-BMO assumption on this weight, we obtain the required regularity and extend to the three-dimensional pinned setting the metastability picture previously established for the homogeneous model.

title: Detectability of an orbital-angular-momentum-based gravitational wave detector
summary: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) of light provides a new approach to probing gravitational waves (GWs) through transitions between OAM states. Here, we assess the detectability of an OAM-based GW detector by developing a readout scheme and evaluating its noise budget over the frequency range from $1~\mathrm{mHz}$ to $100~\mathrm{Hz}$, including laser-intensity noise, laser-phase noise, mode-impurity noise, and shot noise. For a symmetric superposition OAM state, the GW-induced transition amplitudes satisfy $α_+=-α_-^*$, whereas the noise-induced mode-crosstalk coefficients obey $n_+=n_-^*$. Hence, the GW-induced signal forms a differential-mode contribution, while laser-intensity and mode-impurity noises enter as common-mode contributions, enabling their suppression by the balanced detection. Under a fixed beam-waist constraint, a shorter arm permits a larger paraxial parameter, reducing the equivalent angular-noise strain sensitivity. We adopt an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $γ=0.1$, a laser power incident on the beam splitter of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, and a wavelength of $λ_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$. Using representative noise spectra, we find that, for GWs from an equal-mass binary black hole with source-frame component masses of $M_{\mathrm{src}}=10^{4}\,M_{\odot}$ at redshift $z=1$, balanced detection yields an SNR of $24.7$ for an imbalance parameter of $ε=10^{-3}$ and $239$ for $ε=10^{-5}$, with the sensitivity approaching the shot-noise limit in the latter case. These results highlight the importance of a compact optical configuration and strong common-mode rejection for realizing an OAM-based GW detector.

title: Distance to integrability and complexity
summary: We consider nearest-neighbour interactions on spin-1/2 chains. We find the full set of integrable models of this form and apply a numerical algorithm to determine the "closest" integrable model for a given Hamiltonian. This allows us to define a model-independent distance to integrability. We show that standard measures of chaos interpolate between integrable and chaotic values with increasing values of this distance. However, there is a large variation across models and the distance to integrability provides additional information not directly provided by these diagnostics.

title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
summary: Crystal-generation models can explore compositions and atomic arrangements beyond a fixed set of crystal prototypes, but their usefulness for a specific materials family depends on whether the generated structures retain the defining topology and whether their predicted properties remain reliable across the sampled chemistry. Here, a pretrained diffusion model is used to generate candidate ABX$_3$ perovskites and to examine their structural, chemical and electronic-property distributions. A connectivity-based filter distinguishes three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskites from structures that share the same nominal ABX$_3$ stoichiometry. The accepted set contains substantial B-site multiplicity, including ordered double-perovskite configurations that are inaccessible to the two-prototype substitution reference used here. The generated set is enriched in chloride-, bromide- and iodide-containing compositions relative to the Materials Project, while all generated B-site elements are already represented in that database. On the downstream MP-trained ALIGNN scale, the predicted bandgap distribution is shifted towards 1.4 eV, but the target-window fraction (8.2\%) is close to the MP reference fraction (7.3\%); the separate MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources prevent this comparison from establishing target-condition enrichment. An ALIGNN model performs well on a formula-grouped random test split but does not outperform a constant baseline on a deliberately severe B-site-disjoint test. First-principles calculations on six generated structures show that relaxation can alter structural classification and that predicted and calculated gaps can differ appreciably. These results identify both the chemical-space coverage offered by crystal diffusion and the structural and predictive checks needed before its outputs can be treated as materials candidates.

title: Universality of Large-Scale Geometry For Critical Random-Cluster Models
summary: The understanding of the behaviour of critical lattice models in two dimensions has made immense progress in the past couple of decades, with conformal invariance as its conjectured end goal. We consider here the critical random-cluster model (or FK-percolation) on a large class of graphs --- namely bi-periodic isoradial graphs --- with cluster-weight~$q \in [1,4]$. Following up on the establishment of rotational invariance at criticality in \cite{Rotation}, we prove that the large scale behaviour of these models is asymptotically the same on all such graphs. These include the critical homogeneous models on the square, triangular and hexagonal lattices.

title: Wide-field search for submicrosecond optical and gamma transients as manifestation of primordial black holes evaporation with the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array
summary: We demonstrated in our papers [Panov, 2021; Panov,2025), that the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array physics, originally designed for research in cosmic rays and ultra-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy, can also be used for wide-field searches for very rare submicrosecond optical transients of astrophysical origin. The papers \cite{PANOV-2021,PANOV-2025} presented the results of the first four seasons of optical transient searches (2018--2022) and the resulting upper limits on the flux of corresponding events. The present paper presents data processing from two new seasons of optical transient searches (2022--2024). This paper further develops a method for searching for narrow spatiotemporal groups of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays (above 100\,TeV). Since the evaporation of relic black holes can be accompanied by both by the emission of a short light pulse and by a flash of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays, a multimessenger technique for searching for black hole evaporation was in fact implemented in this work, where two different methods are implemented within a single instrument. The search for narrow spatiotemporal groups of gamma-rays was carried out in time windows of 1000\,$μ$s, 100\,$μ$s, and 6\,$μ$s. Since narrow groups of gamma were not detected, the upper limit on their frequency were obtained as $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$. The upper limit on the number of submicrosecond optical transients have also been updated: $10^{-4}\mathrm{erg/s/cm}^2$ as $5\cdot10^{-4}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$.

title: A microscopic stochastic field theory for nonlinear pomeron--odderon evolution based on a Doi--Peliti framework
summary: We construct a reaction-based microscopic realisation of nonlinear pomeron--odderon evolution in rapidity and impact-parameter space. Using the Doi--Peliti formalism, we derive the master equations, their operator representation, the exact hierarchy of factorial moments, and the coherent-state functional integral. The construction admits normalised complex configuration weights while retaining the algebraic conservation law of the gain--loss generator. Pomeron branching and merging yield the complex logistic equation \cite{Kohara:2026} under mean-field factorisation. Pomeron-catalysed odderon branching and ternary odderon fusion provide an odd sector whose evolution is driven by the pomeron background. Without transverse diffusion, the resulting equations admit an analytical solution in quadrature, allowing us to examine amplification, phase evolution, and nonlinear regulation. A specified matching between the first moments and the even and odd scattering profiles connects this evolution to elastic-scattering observables. Illustrative initial conditions produce a nonmonotonic forward ratio and a splitting between the $pp$ and $p\bar p$ channels, while the interference near a diffractive minimum remains sensitive to the relative phases and transverse profiles. These examples illustrate the effective dynamics without constituting a fit to data or a general proof of scattering unitarity.

title: Charge-Order pattern in $κ$-BEDT-TTF salts: A model independent, selection rule approach
summary: A well known vibrational selection rule is invoked to determine the charge order (CO) pattern displayed by the most interesting members of the widely studied class of $κ$-BEDT-TTF salts and their molecular analogues. The selection rule indicates that an easily identifiable Raman band should be present if intra-dimer charge disproportionation occurs, constituting a sort of model independent ``litmus test''. The absence of such a band in the available Raman spectra of $κ$-BEDT-TTF salts exhibiting static of fluctuating CO, strongly suggests that the CO pattern involves inter-dimer CO, in contrast with the universally accepted intra-dimer disprortionation. This paper therefore poses a challenge for the theoretical modeling of the concerned salts: either the lack of the Raman band sensitive to intra-dimer CO pattern is explained, or the modeling of the multivariate, unique physical properties of these $κ$-phase salts (spin frustration, electronic ferroelectricity etc.) has to start from the perspective of a different ground state.

title: Multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function
comment: 34 pages. Based on the second author's MSc thesis
summary: We construct multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function as nested products of overlap coefficients between eigenfunctions of twisted primitive elements in representations of the modular double of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. The construction is a hyperbolic counterpart of the nested multivariate Askey--Wilson polynomials and functions. Using iterated coproducts, we derive four systems of difference equations for which these multivariate functions are joint eigenfunctions. The four systems correspond to the two sets of variables and the two step sizes $iw_1$ and $iw_2$, which are interchanged by modular duality. We also prove that Ruijsenaars' one-variable transform is unitary in the parameter regime required for the construction, for positive as well as complex conjugate $w_1,w_2$. A two-sided normalization of the kernel separates the input and output weights, so that iterating one-variable transforms yields unitary multivariate transforms with explicit inverse and Plancherel formulas.

title: The Devil Went Down to de Sitter: Divergent Effective Field Theory Expansions in Cosmology
summary: Effective field theories (EFTs) in de Sitter space, and in accelerating cosmologies more generally, must capture phenomena absent in flat space, most notably long-range correlations generated by spontaneous particle production. When heavy physics is integrated out in such time-dependent backgrounds, these effects leave an imprint on the EFT expansion: even at tree level, this is generically an asymptotic rather than convergent series. This is not a failure of EFT. The large-order behavior of the expansion coefficients encodes physical information inaccessible at any finite order, so cosmological EFTs contain hidden data. Using resurgence analysis, we show how this information can be systematically extracted to recover exact and non-perturbative predictions from the perturbative expansion. In the example we study, the resurgent completion is naturally organized in terms of the de Sitter $S$-matrix. This leads us to conjecture a prescription for extracting $S$-matrix data from cosmological EFTs in general. The framework extends to any setting where particle production, or a similar non-perturbative phenomenon, renders the EFT expansion asymptotic. A longer companion paper will provide a more detailed and pedagogical treatment.

title: Zero mode, Zero influence: Spatial-derivative coupling in particle detectors
summary: It is common in particle detector models in cavity QED to often omit zero modes or assume their state, compromising causality or introducing ambiguity in their predictions. We show that spatial-derivative coupling eliminates both problems. For free massless scalar fields in static periodic or Neumann cavities of any spatial dimension, cavity-frame spatial derivatives annihilate the zero-mode operator while preserving microcausality. Detector dynamics and entanglement harvesting then depend only on the reduced detector-oscillator state, nonperturbatively and even with initial correlations with the zero mode. Time derivatives and moving-detector rest-frame spatial derivatives can retain zero-mode state dependence not compromising causality. Realized through current coupling in superconducting circuits, spatial-derivative coupling thus makes zero-mode state assumptions unnecessary.

title: Three-Dimensional FDTD Simulation of Superconducting Terahertz Emitters Using an Effective Medium Approximation
summary: Compact and tunable terahertz (THz) sources with controllable polarization are sought for high-speed links, spectroscopy, and imaging. In superconducting THz emitters based on a cuprate Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+δ}$, which have the potential to satisfy such properties, modeling often relies on heavy nonlinear solvers or empirical isotropic dielectrics, obscuring anisotropy, plasma response, and bias dependence. We derive an anisotropic, dispersive effective permittivity from the Lawrence-Doniach model for a layered superconductor and implement it as a user-defined material in a commercial Finite-difference Time-domain (FDTD) solver. Simulations of two device geometries reproduce linearly polarized emission from a rectangular mesa and low-axial-ratio (near-circular) emission from a truncated square mesa. This CAD-ready workflow links superconducting theory to device design, enabling rapid searches and parameter optimization for next-generation THz sources.

title: Bilateral Christoffel-Geronimus-Uvarov formulas for mixed-type orthogonality on algebraic supports
summary: Christoffel-type determinant formulas construct both normalized polynomial families and their reproducing kernel for mixed-type orthogonality in several variables after independent rational matrix transformations on the two arguments. The pairing may have a rectangular matrix of functionals, with separate degree bounds on each component, and may be supported on an algebraic variety. The reduced matrices are calculated from the original biorthogonal polynomials, rational moments, polynomial division and the masses left free by division; their nonvanishing determinants characterize existence and uniqueness. For measure pairings the rational data are expressed by Cauchy and multivariate Fantappie transforms. Exact dimension counts incorporate the four matrix factors and the relations of the support. For normal degree-ordered original families and fixed factors, when the component degrees on each side differ by a bounded amount and the normalization dimension grows at most like one degree layer, the resulting orders are bounded on curves and grow at most linearly on surfaces. For pairings allowing scalar factors to move between arguments, called balanced pairings, an exact obstruction determines whether a bilateral mass decomposes into unilateral masses when the denominators act injectively. Residue duality provides coordinates for division and mass quotients on integral curves, including singular points, and on the finite surface quotients specified here. Explicit singular-curve families retain nondegenerate residue pairings as denominator zeros coalesce. Positive congruences admit a further reduction by orthogonal projection, while balanced pairings give simultaneous intertwining identities for all coordinate multiplication matrices.

title: Tests of an EP-Preserving Wake Force
summary: A universal quadratic coupling of ultralight scalar dark matter to ordinary matter preserves the weak equivalence principle for unscreened point particles. A finite test body is nevertheless not a passive probe: it distorts the scalar field that accelerates it. We show that this field distortion produces a differential acceleration between concentric test masses, even when their microscopic coupling is universal. We calculate this signal including how each test mass distorts the field acting on the other, deriving the weak-screening limit and extending the calculation to stronger screening using concentric spherical layers. Applying the model to MICROSCOPE, we find differential signals in both its equivalence-principle sensor SUEP, whose test masses have different compositions, and its reference sensor SUREF, whose test masses have the same composition. We combine both sensors with the dark matter wake near Earth to recast the published MICROSCOPE measurements. Within this model, existing measurements probe scalar masses up to approximately $8 \times 10^{-9}\,$eV and couplings below the supernova bound. An analysis using the additional frequency components of the scalar signal could extend the mass reach and probe couplings below the BBN bound.

title: Quantum superposition of Cosmic String spacetimes
summary: Since the quantum nature of spacetime is anticipated by a theory of Quantum Gravity, the possibility of spacetime superposition would be a natural consequence. This spacetime interference phenomena could bring us some clues about what effects could be expected over quantum fields and their interaction with matter. In this article, we investigate the effect of the superposition of a Cosmic String spacetime on the Unruh-De Witt detector. This is of interest as the spacetimes possess flat geometry but non-trivial topology. We analyze the effect of the interference of a Cosmic String with different topological charge over the Unruh-De Witt detector response function to vacuum fluctuations. We obtain some quantum interference effects, due to the superposition of spacetimes, which would be absent if a classical probabilistic mixture of spacetimes would be considered. In this manner, we obtain real physical consequences that would be indications of a Quantum Gravity phenomena.

title: High-order concentric hopfions in a helimagnet
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, bilingual: English (edited machine translation), Russian (primary)
summary: Magnetic hopfions are three-dimensional topological solitons: ``knots'' in the vector field of magnetization of magnetically ordered materials, which are a key element of the three-dimensional spintronics emerging today. In this work, a simple analytical model for a new type of magnetic hopfions --- ``concentric'' ones --- is constructed and solved. Their size and equilibrium energy are estimated, their stability region on the magnetic phase diagram of a helimagnet is mapped out, and the requirements for materials admitting equilibrium concentric hopfions with high Hopf index on a uniformly magnetized background are determined.

title: A Hierarchical direct solver for Lippmann-Schwinger equations based on boundary traces
summary: A high-order hierarchical direct solver for variable-media scattering in two dimensions is presented. Standard discretizations for these problems produce dense linear systems that are commonly solved iteratively, requiring a new global solve for each incident field. The method proposed here instead constructs a reusable scattering operator for the inhomogeneous medium, based on a hierarchical subdivision of the computational domain. First, high-accuracy leaf scattering operators are built from discretized local integral equations. Up the hierarchy, neighboring boxes are merged to build the scattering operators for successively larger boxes. A key feature of the method is that each scattering operator is represented as a map of incoming traces to outgoing traces. Consequently, volume unknowns appear only in the leaf computations; all higher levels of the hierarchy operate entirely on boundary traces. The hierarchical solver is presented first at the continuum level and discretized only afterward using high-order local volume quadrature, polynomial trace representations, and boundary integral techniques. For a discretization involving $N$ degrees of freedom, the method requires $O(N^{3/2})$ work and $O(N\log N)$ storage to build all scattering operators. Once these are available, any incoming field can be processed at cost $O(N)$ if only the outgoing field is required, and cost $O(N\log N)$ if the full field is required. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy on a range of challenging scattering problems including cavities, back-scattering, limited regularity, and high wavenumber, that pose significant challenges to iterative methods.

title: A local action for Kodaira--Spencer gravity
comment: 28 pages, produced in collaboration with Claude
summary: A local action is given for Kodaira--Spencer gravity by solving a constraint on the complex structure deformation of a Calabi--Yau threefold in terms of a $(1,1)$ form as the new gravity field. The gauge algebra becomes a genuine $L_{\infty}$ algebra based on a Courant algebroid, while the gravity field and its linearized gauge transformations coincide with those of double field theory. On a real three-dimensional slice, the free action reduces to the Fierz--Pauli action for massless spin-2 plus the Kalb--Ramond action for a B-field. Non-linearly, the theory carries parity-odd interactions with three derivatives, and it is gauge invariant without a level-matching constraint, in this sense defining an unconstrained double field theory. The full theory is encoded in a cyclic $L_{\infty}$ algebra, for which a double copy interpretation is given.

title: Exact scalarization thresholds and onset laws for a nonminimally coupled scalar field on the Ellis wormhole
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Ancillary files contain the numerical codes
summary: We study a real scalar field nonminimally coupled to curvature on a fixed Ellis wormhole background. The scalar perturbation decouples at linear order, and the substitution $ x=a \tan z $ reduces its static radial equation to a trigonometric Pöschl-Teller problem. This yields the exact threshold spectrum $ ζ_{n\ell}=(n+\ell+1)^2/2 $, closed-form Gegenbauer profiles, and an exact count of negative radial eigenvalues in each angular sector. The s-wave thresholds are zero-energy resonances at which the growth rate rises linearly, whereas the $ \ell \geq1\ $ threshold states are square integrable and the growth rate rises as a square root. At the first threshold we also obtain the next-order term, $ σa=(π/4)g-(3π/16)g^2+O(g^3) $ with $g=2ζ-1 $. For a probe field with quartic self-interaction, we show that no nontrivial spherical static solution exists for $ζ\leq1/2 $ and derive local branch expansions near the s-wave thresholds. Numerical evolutions are consistent with saturation on the nodeless branch. These nonlinear results refer to the probe-field model; they do not establish the existence or stability of fully backreacted scalarized wormholes.

title: Radiofrequency plasma spheroidization of lightweight complex concentrated superalloy Al10Nb20Ta15Ti30V5Zr20
summary: Recent advances in additive manufacturing (AM) have significantly increased the demand for high-quality metal powders with tailored composition. For refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCA) preparing such powders by conventional metallurgical method remains challenging due to their high melting point and chemical reactivity. In this paper, we present a method to produce spherical RCCA powders (here Al10Nb20Ta15Ti30V5Zr20) via mechanical alloying followed by radio-frequency inductively coupled plasma spheroidization. The resulting powder is suitable for AM processes because of its spherical morphology and a microstructure consisting of major BCC phases with local B2 phase. Complex carbide formation was studied by 3D atom probe tomography.

title: A closed formula for the Poisson cohomology of scalar Dubrovin-Novikov brackets in arbitrary dimension
summary: The structure of the Poisson cohomology groups for scalar Poisson brackets of Dubrovin-Novikov type with $D$ independent variables has been first described in arXiv:1512.05744 ; in that work, a complete dimensional counting was provided for $D=2$, and some numerical results exhibited for $D=3$, $D=4$. Here, we prove a formula for the dimensional counting of the Poisson cohomology for arbitrary $D$. Moreover, we show how to obtain canonical representatives for each cohomology class.

summary: It is common in particle detector models in cavity QED to often omit zero modes or assume their state, compromising causality or introducing ambiguity in their predictions. Realized through current coupling in superconducting circuits, spatial-derivative coupling thus makes zero-mode state assumptions unnecessary.

title: The Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem and Dynamical Love Number in Schwarzschild Black Holes
summary: We study the real-time response of a Schwarzschild black hole in the Hartle-Hawking state to an external massless scalar field. Using a complexified radial contour to represent the Schwinger-Keldysh closed time path, we describe dissipation, thermal fluctuations and conservative tidal response within a common framework. Before performing tidal matching, we derive the equilibrium fluctuation-dissipation relation directly from the radial construction for every scalar multipole at arbitrary real frequency. In the low-frequency tidal expansion, we recover the known relation between the logarithmic running of the conservative dynamical Love coefficient at order $ω^2$ and the leading dissipative response at order $ω$. We explain how the same leading absorptive coefficient enters both relations at low frequency and trace the unit coefficient of the running relation to the Schwarzschild horizon slope. In the Hartle-Hawking state, this common coefficient relates the logarithmic running directly to the zero-frequency thermal noise. Kubo-Martin-Schwinger analyticity determines the thermal noise from the dissipative response, whereas the near-zone radial equation and tidal matching determine the conservative logarithmic running.

title: Efficient Interpolation of the Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian at Arbitrary Momenta
summary: We develop an efficient reciprocal-space method to reconstruct the static Bethe-Salpeter (BSE) Hamiltonian at arbitrary crystal momenta from coarse first-principles grids. Bloch states are interpolated within an optimally smooth Wannier subspace, while the screened Coulomb interaction is reconstructed from the dielectric response. This decouples the electron-hole transition momenta and transferred momentum from the underlying ab initio sampling. We benchmark the method on monolayer hBN, monolayer MoS$_2$, and bulk GaAs against explicit ab initio calculations, finding excellent agreement for dense-grid Bloch states, dielectric screening, and BSE optical spectra. Furthermore, our cost analysis estimates speedups of up to $22\times$ on the grids considered here. Arbitrary transferred-momentum sampling gives direct access to the long-wavelength exciton dispersion: in hBN and MoS$_2$, we resolve the nonanalytic behaviour induced by long-range electron-hole exchange at momenta well below the spacing of practical uniform grids. For bulk GaAs, locally refined transition-momentum sampling yields a converged binding energy for the threefold-degenerate lowest exciton, in close agreement with experiment and reference calculations, using far fewer BSE points than conventional uniform meshes. As the present framework provides exciton energies and amplitudes at arbitrary crystal momenta, it opens the way to incorporating ab initio excitonic effects into nonlocal electron-phonon vertices and to extensions towards exciton-phonon interactions and nonequilibrium exciton dynamics.

title: Exact scalarization thresholds and onset laws for a nonminimally coupled scalar field on the Ellis wormhole
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Ancillary files contain the numerical codes

title: Quantum Black Holes in Non-Linear Electrodynamics
summary: Techniques of AdS/CFT correspondence and braneworld holography have proven to be a useful tool for solving the problem of semi-classical gravity where quantum matter provides the back-reaction to classical spacetime geometry. In this paper, we apply this approach to Einstein gravity coupled to RegMax nonlinear electrodynamics and construct novel type of charged quantum black holes. We then discuss their thermodynamics and horizon structure.

title: Holonomy classification, gyroscope precession, and Landau levels in Gödel-type spacetimes and their superfluid analog
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures. Verification scripts (Python/SymPy) and figure scripts (Python, MATLAB) available as ancillary files
summary: We derive the parallel-transport holonomies of circles centered on the symmetry axis in the homogeneous Gödel-type family of Rebouças and Tiomno, which includes the Gödel universe, the causal member with $m^2=4Ω^2$, and the Som--Raychaudhuri limit. The holonomy is governed by a single invariant $Δ(r)$, whose sign determines whether the Lorentz transformation is elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic. We determine the number of parabolic radii across the family and prove that, whenever the azimuthal circles become closed timelike curves (CTCs), the chronology radius satisfies $Δ(r_c)=-\cosh(mr_c)<0$. We also express this invariant in terms of Killing-vector scalars, derive the vector and spinor Wilson loops, give the exact condition for trivial holonomy after a finite number of turns, and analyze Fermi--Walker transport on circular CTCs. Finally, we discuss an analogy with the effective metric of a rotating superfluid, valid under stated conditions, and derive exact expressions for the radial $L^2$ localization of Klein--Gordon Landau modes relative to the Som--Raychaudhuri chronology radius. The geometric results are exact within the metric family considered; the discussion of the analog system relies on the validity of a coarse-grained effective description.

title: Spontaneous Chirality and Collective Chern Bands in a Dipole-Conserving Bose System
summary: We demonstrate spontaneous chiral dipole order and an isolated collective Chern band in a time-reversal-symmetric microscopic bosonic lattice model with exact dipole-moment conservation. In a controlled large-occupation limit at zero temperature, frustrated dipole exchange and three-particle conversion stabilize two time-reversed chiral condensates. The two dipole Goldstone modes remain gapless, while a separate finite-frequency band carries Chern numbers $-1$ and $+1$ in the opposite domains. We trace this topology to complex mode couplings in the chiral background that gap finite-frequency Dirac crossings. Site-resolved density drives preserve dipole-moment conservation and reconstruct the band Chern number from band-resolved absorption spectra in the quadratic theory.

title: Quantum Diffusion and the Block-Size Crossover in the Block Anderson Model
comment: 117 pages, 2 figures. A short video overview is available: https://youtu.be/CLAtq3mPhNU?si=so7PnIZfMknlsqvS
summary:
We study the block Anderson Hamiltonian \(H_L=λΨ_L+\mathcal V\) on the discrete torus \((\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d\), \(d\geq2\), where \(Ψ_L\) is the nearest-neighbor Laplacian and \(\mathcal V\) consists of independent \(W^d\times W^d\) GOE blocks. In the weak-disorder limit \(λ\to\infty\), we establish an entrywise local law, a spatial scaling limit for the squared resolvent entries, time-averaged dynamical delocalization, and lower bounds on the localization length of most bulk eigenfunctions. Particularly, we allow the block size to be fixed or grow above a polylogarithmic threshold. In sufficiently large polynomial volumes, the dynamical estimates hold for \(C_δ(λ+W/λ)\leq T\leq λ^{1+κ_d^{\rm BA}-δ}\), with a dimension-dependent exponent \(κ_d^{\rm BA}>0\), and the spreading scale is \(\sqrt{(λ^3+λW)T}\). This identifies a transition at \(W\asympλ^2\) between \(λ^{3/2}\sqrt T\) and \(\sqrt{λWT}\).
  The proof combines Gaussian moment estimates with deterministic stability of a matrix Dyson equation. A partial Bloch transform handles fixed blocks, while scalar reduction controls growing blocks. A Feshbach--Schur reduction of the block \(T\)-equation separates a single scalar diffusion mode from the stable internal cell modes. A renewal expansion and exact cell counting give a positive representation of the diffusion coefficient and control the fourth moment uniformly across the block-size transition. Notably, our argument does not require an enumeration of Feynman diagrams.

title: How tightly can PBH abundance information constrain scalar-induced gravitational waves?
summary: Primordial black hole (PBH) abundances and scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) probe the same primordial fluctuations through different physical weights. We examine the predictive power of precise synthetic information on absolute PBH abundances over a finite stellar-mass interval, together with an exact total abundance and external population bounds. For Gaussian perturbations under a fixed quantum chromodynamics (QCD) formation prescription, two smooth, symmetric lognormal spectra satisfy the same abundance conditions while producing nonproportional leading-order SIGW spectra. The two spectra differ by about 20% when averaged over the lower of two adjacent nanohertz windows but by nearly a factor of 60 in the higher-frequency window, so the difference cannot be represented by a single rescaling of the gravitational-wave background. Peak position and width compensate with amplitude in the abundance calculation, while the higher-frequency window draws almost all its energy from scalar-mode pairs with both wavenumbers above the primordial peak. Under the principal abundance benchmark, local finite-width components yield larger contrasts at a fixed nanohertz frequency through distinct mode couplings under both the QCD and stochastic peak-curvature formation prescriptions. For a separately generated population, extending mass information over most of its abundance restricts the lognormal peak-position and width compensation and reduces the higher-window contrast, while the unequal window responses persist. These results show why joint PBH-SIGW inference must propagate primordial shapes compatible with the PBH abundance information rather than assign one tensor template to a single abundance fit.

title: Large $N$ limit of the ratio of Lukyanov integrals
summary: We study the large-$N$ asymptotics of ratios of Lukyanov integrals for fixed real coupling $b\geq1$. Our approach uses their biorthogonal ensemble structure and vector Riemann--Hilbert techniques. Under stated analytic hypotheses, we derive the logarithmic ratio through its constant term, which is expressed by a Fredholm determinant. The expansion is locally uniform in the real parameter $α$ and is formulated separately for even and odd particle numbers. We verify the hypotheses for the correction defined by the physical ground-state thermodynamic Bethe ansatz. The relation to quantum-field-theoretic one-point functions is discussed separately.

title: Melting noncoplanar order on the square-kagome lattice: Chiral, flat-band, and staggered spin liquids from projective symmetry
comment: 29 pages, 9 figures, 10 tables, and Supplemental Material
summary: Noncoplanar magnetic orders carry a scalar spin chirality, and their melting by quantum fluctuations has been proposed as a route to chiral spin liquids. We ask what this route can produce on the square-kagome lattice, where couplings across the octagons stabilize noncoplanar cuboc and conical orders. We classify the fermionic spin liquids of this lattice by their projective symmetry groups, identify the symmetry class into which each noncoplanar order would melt, and compare candidate states with Gutzwiller-projected wave functions. A magnetic selection rule constrains the route: the chirality of every cuboc and conical order alternates in space, so a liquid that keeps the symmetry of its parent order has zero Chern number and no spontaneous thermal Hall response. A Chern state can descend only from uniformly chiral orders, and the regular ones we find need ferromagnetic bow-tie couplings. The energetics do not favor a chiral liquid either: among the projected wave functions we compare, a cuboc1-ordered state is lowest for strong cross-octagon couplings, and nonchiral states, a valence-bond crystal or a time-reversal-symmetric liquid, for weaker ones. The two inequivalent site orbits shape the spinons: a relative time-reversal sign between them pins flat bands to the Fermi level, and because the translations of $p4mm$ are not commutators, staggered chiral liquids exist, which are absent on sixfold-symmetric lattices.

title: A unifying view of averaging for wave-mean flow decomposition
comment: 45 pages, 9 figures. Submitted for peer review
summary: Geophysical flows are routinely decomposed into mean flow and waves, and the procedure used determines how the motion is divided between the two. Ideally, the wave and mean motions of interest evolve on distinct timescales, in which case they can be separated by taking an infinite-time average over all wave periods. Individual waves average away, while exactly resonant interactions contribute to the averaged dynamics because they are steady on the fast timescale. We generalize this averaging to finite windows, yielding a family of decompositions that additionally retain near-resonant interactions whose phases do not fully cancel over the time window. Such averaging necessarily invokes a choice of reference frame; the same flow averaged in two frames may yield mean flows differing by a drift. The averaging formulation developed here enables us to express Stokes drift through resonant and near-resonant interactions, confirming the intuition that it is a slow quantity generated by fast waves and revealing a coherent near-resonant contribution generally present in Stokes drift calculated over finite time from broadband wave fields. We use the fast-wave evolution underlying the exact average to define both the wave reference frame, in which the fast phase is steady, and a wave-frame average. We cast familiar Eulerian and Lagrangian averages and this wave-frame average in a common form to further illustrate how the chosen frame determines which motions enter the mean. This view of averaging provides a common basis for comparing decompositions and choosing among them according to the physical processes one seeks to isolate.

title: Cuscuton Fifth Force: Implications of Non-Dynamical Scalars for Structure Growth
summary: The cuscuton is a scalar field that obeys a constraint rather than an evolution equation, so it modifies gravity without adding a propagating scalar degree of freedom. We study the cosmology of effective cuscuton theory when matter is minimally coupled in the Jordan frame, and therefore conformally coupled to the cuscuton in the Einstein-frame. We derive the background and linear perturbation equations and show that the algebraic cuscuton response mediates a fifth force even though the scalar itself does not propagate. The same conformal factor also changes Einstein-frame particle masses and the friction of matter perturbations, tying the strength and sign of the force to the background evolution rather than to an independent coupling. We study a power-law family of models which contain both tracking solutions and sign-switching solutions; in the latter the effective cuscuton density runs from negative during matter domination to a positive, cosmological-constant-like value today. Using a modified version of CLASS, including the induced particle-mass dependence of recombination, we illustrate the corresponding changes to CMB temperature and linear matter power spectra for benchmark models, without fitting to data. In the strongest benchmarks the fifth force changes the effective gravitational coupling on sub-horizon scales by about one percent, smaller than the accompanying changes to the matter power spectrum and the acoustic scale. For the sign-switching solutions this change is negative over most of cosmic history, so a non-propagating field can weaken rather than strengthen gravitational attraction.

title: Unitary implementability of Darboux transformations
summary: We investigate the unitary implementability of the canonical transformations corresponding to Darboux transformations in the Hamiltonian formalism recently developed for gauge invariant perturbations of nonrotating black holes. Starting from the formalism in the black hole interior, we demonstrate that these canonical transformations are unitarily implementable under general conditions on the effective potentials appearing in the master equations of the perturbations. We also show that the privileged massless Fock representation of the perturbative variables selected by admitting (Heisenberg) unitary dynamics, employed in our quantization, is not unitarily equivalent to the simple massless representation of the master variables satisfying the effective Regge-Wheeler equation. This highlights the importance of the choice of master variables in which the quantum representation is initially defined. Furthermore, we show that not all such choices of variables possessing unitarily implementable dynamics can be reached through Darboux transformations, but rather through more general canonical transformations. These results advance our understanding of the relationship between well-established classical relations in black hole perturbation theory and their quantum representations, explaining how isospectral Darboux transformations can be extended to include all the infinitely many possible values of the angular momentum such that they are unitarily implementable in a quantum field theory context.

title: Excited-state-induced nonlinearity and polarity reversals in the thermocurrent through a quantum dot
summary: Quantum dots are electrically tuneable thermal machines capable of both energy harvesting and cooling at the nanoscale in the cryogenic regime. At large thermal biases, their thermoelectric transport shows a complex behaviour, including additional extrema and polarity reversals in the thermocurrent. Though these asymmetries and nonlinearities directly affect rectification and power conversion, their origin has not been studied systematically. We address this through measurements and modelling of a single GaAs/AlGaAs quantum dot whose source is heated by white-noise excitation. Using Pauli master equation for sequential tunnelling through a two-level dot, retaining the full Fermi distributions of both leads, distinct tunnel rates for the two levels, and relaxation between them, we show that the excited state acts as a second transport channel which competes with the ground-state contribution. Strong excited-state coupling combined with slow relaxation produces polarity reversals in the thermocurrent; without both, the excited state yields only additional extrema and an amplitude asymmetry across the charge degeneracy point. Experimentally, as the source temperature increases, an additional extremum emerges in the thermocurrent which develops into a polarity reversal. Using the excited-state level spacing and ground-state tunnel rate obtained independently from pulsed-gate and bias spectroscopies, the model reproduces the positions of the observed extrema and their amplitudes to within a factor of about three, placing the device in the regime of slow relaxation and strong excited-state coupling. Our results establish thermocurrent line-shape as a probe of excited-state tunnelling and relaxation in quantum dots. Excited states, often treated as a minor correction, can dominate quantum-dot thermoelectric transport far from equilibrium.

title: A note on the quantization of M2-branes on local Calabi-Yau manifolds
summary: In this note we present a detailed computation of the BPS states from M2-branes wrapping 2-cycles in local Calabi-Yau manifolds, at the level of brane quantization. For the cases of local Calabi-Yau threefolds, the supersymmetric quantum mechanics is the 1d $\mathcal{N}=4$ non-linear sigma model. We achieve systematic, physical interpretations of refined Gopakumar-Vafa (GV) invariants, first for the curve classes with fixed geometric genus, and then for curves whose geometric genus jumps. The BPS states of 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories are interpreted from the local geometries, which are presented in a number of case studies. In particular, we compute the refined GV invariants for generalized conifolds, local CY3 giving 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories and a singularity whose crepant resolution contains a singular divisor. For the cases of local Calabi-Yau fourfolds, we point out the supersymmetric quantum mechanics is of type $\mathcal{N}=2B$. We set up the framework for studying M2-branes wrapping 2-cycles, and discuss a few cases of M2-brane wrapping genus-0 curves with this new approach.

title: Cosmological rigidity via $p$-harmonic temporal functions
summary: We prove a splitting theorem for cosmological spacetimes which admit a globally $p$-harmonic Cauchy temporal function for some $p < 1$, without making any use of timelike lines. In Bartnik's context of cosmological and timelike geodesically complete spacetimes, we establish a Liouville-type unboundedness result which shows that globally $p$-harmonic temporal functions, $p < 1$, are necessarily Cauchy temporal. Moreover, using the theory of elliptic PDEs, we show that locally Lipschitz $p$-harmonic temporal functions with $p < 1$ are in fact smooth. Altogether, our work reduces the resolution of Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture to the global weak solvability of the $p$-d'Alembert equation for some $p < 1$ in the class of locally Lipschitz temporal functions.

title: Excess inner-horizon entropy and the thermodynamics of Kerr formation
summary: \noindent We develop a charge-matched thermodynamic framework for the regular rotating black-hole family underlying an exact model of Kerr formation. Since the Kerr endpoint already possesses a Cauchy horizon, hidden entropy is identified with the excess inner-horizon area relative to Kerr at fixed mass $M$ and angular momentum $J=Ma$: $\Sexc=π[h_c^2-(r_-^{\Kerr})^2]$, where $h_c$ is the regular inner-horizon radius and $r_-^{\Kerr}=M-\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$. Under regularity and interior-profile assumptions, we prove $r_-^{\Kerr}<h_c<h$ and establish the sharp bound $0<\Sexc<4πM\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$. The Schwarzschild limit yields $\Sexc=πh_c^2$, while $\Sexc=0$ at the Kerr endpoint. The Kerr reference entropy satisfies $S_+^{\Kerr}+S_-^{\Kerr}=4πM^2$, so rotation redistributes its two-horizon contributions at fixed mass. For the time-dependent model, we derive exact evolution equations for the inner root and $\Sexc$, interpreted as root-bookkeeping identities unless the roots are established as dynamical horizons. In the minimal $N=1$ trajectory, the apparent pole at $n=2$ is removable in the mass profile, giving a logarithmic continuation of the root equation, although the stationary curvature is singular there. The stationary Ricci-scalar density is locally absolutely integrable for $-1<n\leq2$, with the Kerr endpoint $n=-1$ treated separately. Minkowski breaking occurs at $n=0$, independently of inner-horizon disappearance. Quasi-extremal regular configurations approach, but cannot attain, the entropy bound without losing a regular Killing horizon.

title: Active Jarzynski and Crooks Relations for Driven Jump-Diffusions
summary: Non-conservative active driving breaks detailed balance in non-Gaussian jump-diffusions, obscuring the connection between external protocol work, housekeeping dissipation, and free-energy differences. Here, we establish exact finite-time fluctuation relations for driven Markov jump-diffusions---encompassing infinite-activity Lévy processes---by comparing path probabilities under the forward and current-reversed dual dynamics relative to the instantaneous steady state (ISS). We derive a trajectory-level decomposition of total entropy production that cleanly separates transient state relaxation, housekeeping heat, and external protocol driving. When the ISS takes a Gibbsian form, gauge-tilting the dual path measure yields an Active Jarzynski equality, $\langle\exp[-(W+Δs_{\mathrm{act}})]\rangle_{π_0}=e^{-ΔF}$, which incorporates active housekeeping entropy $Δs_{\mathrm{act}}$ alongside mechanical work $W$ and coexists with the conventional Jarzynski equality. Under protocol reversal, this dual framework further reveals an Active Crooks relation, where the asymmetry between forward and reverse work distributions is governed by the conditional exponential average of active dissipation. Our results provide a framework for recovering free-energy differences in driven jump-diffusions with Gibbsian instantaneous steady states and for characterizing active irreversibility through trajectory statistics.

title: Informative Fisher Modes in Neural Networks as a Result of Explicit Symmetry Breaking
summary: Learning in a neural network takes place on a high dimensional, non-convex loss landscape, the Hessian curvature of which dictates the learning dynamics. Despite its high dimensionality, the large number of architectural symmetries explains some of the geometric of this landscape, in particular flat directions, i.e. near-zero modes of the Hessian. These architectural symmetries have therefore been suggested as an organizing principle of deep learning. It remains an open question, though, wether there are additional organizing principles in the remaining degrees of freedom in the learning dynamic. Here we identify task-dependent contingent symmetries as such an additional organizing principle. We show that non-flat learning directions emerge due to explicit breaking of these contingent symmetries. We isolate this symmetry in an analytically solvable minimal model. Furthermore, we show that, by tuning an L2 penalty, signatures of the symmetry breaking become measurable. As a consequence of the same mechanism, adding noise to the data drives the model through a sequence of broken symmetry recoveries in the form of Baik-Ben-Arous-Péché (BBP) transitions. We demonstrate analytically for linear and numerically for deep linear networks that the contingent symmetry group remains explicit, and that the symmetry-breaking mechanism identifies which Hessian modes carry task-specific information. These signatures are measurable without a symmetry-group description and, hence, offer a route to study symmetry breaking as a more general principle in nonlinear networks and other learning systems.

title: Quantum Recovery from Black-Hole Radiation Beyond the Emission Yield
summary: A proposed resolution of the black-hole information paradox must explain which information an outside observer can recover from escaping radiation\cite{Hawking,Page,Hayden,Almheiri}. Environmental memory can return correlations to the source without delivering them to that observer\cite{ChenQi,ChenMemory}. Here we establish a sharp recovery frontier at fixed mean radiation yield for single-excitation channels and realize its qubit limit with an autonomous quantum-memory emitter. Unequal transmissions balance retained coherence against information in failed collection events. A reference--radiation correlation test distinguishes this gain even when the mean collected energy is unchanged. Identical transmission channels instead give the same recovery at matched collection, regardless of their emission timescales. For a broader class of interacting sources, an ordering of collected and inaccessible coupling spectra forbids unassisted quantum transmission irrespective of internal memory. A separate coding example supports a positive rate where uniform transmission at matched actual yield has zero capacity. Together, these results identify what openness must change to assist recovery: the accessible transmission structure. They supply a physically constrained comparison of evaporation mechanisms, separating information delivered to radiation from coherence retained elsewhere or an increase in the collected output.

authors: J. Pacheco B. C. de melo
title: Behavior of the zero modes in the Light-front for pseudo scalar particles: pion case
summary:
Light-front Quantum Field Theory (LFQFT) stands as an
  optimal framework for
  delving into the intricate substructure of hadronic
  bound states. In this study, we employ a
  Light-Front Constituent Quark Model (LFCQM)
  to investigate the pion's internal structure. This model has previously
  demonstrated significant success in describing the properties of pseudoscalar mesons.
  A crucial consideration within the light-front formalism is the dependence on the
  chosen reference frame, stemming from the explicit breaking of covariance. Herein, we meticulously
  analyze the
  contribution of zero modes to the pion's electromagnetic current.
  Subsequently, we explore the impact of these zero modes on observable quantities,
  including electromagnetic form factors, the pion's electromagnetic radius,
  and its weak decay constant, $f_π$.
  Furthermore, we comprehensively investigate the behavior of zero modes and their
  dependence on both the momentum transfer, $Q^2$, and the model's intrinsic parameters,
  such as constituent quark masses ($m_{(q,\bar{q})}$) and the regulator mass ($m_R$).
  Our findings reveal
  a substantial dependence of light-front zero modes on the specific frame employed
  for the calculation of the electromagnetic current. Interestingly, we observe
  that the maximal contribution of the zero mode occurs at a specific
  four-momentum transfer, denoted as $Q^2 = -q^2 = q_Z^{2(Max.)}$.

title: Anomalous response, re-emerging localization-transition and robust corner sates in self-similar peano fractal
summary: Anomalous spectral response from the non-interacting electrons on a peano fractal is recorded within tight-binding framework. It is observed that a minimal off-diagonal anisotropy can modulate the transport characteristics of the lattice. Drastic modification in the nature of the eigenstates has been validated through the workout of level spacing statistics. Further, a two-dimensional quasiperiodic Aubry-André and Harper variation in the overlap integral can invite re-entrant localization-delocalization transition for the self-similar model. This is associated with the possible existence of single-particle mobility edge in the energy landscape. Our results are corroborated by the evaluation of inverse participation ratio, fractal dimension and quantum dynamical response. The spectrum is shown to formulate a quantum butterfly pattern with the frequency of the modulation. Chiral symmetry protected edge states are found to be insensitive with respect to moderate diagonal disorder.

title: Free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses
summary: We compute the limit of free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses with possibly non-convex interaction and couplings satisfying a finite fourth-moment assumption. The couplings need not be Gaussian. The limit is given by a logarithmic-determinant variational formula, equivalently by a finite-dimensional matrix Dyson equation, and its zero-temperature limit yields the ground-state energy. The limiting formulas depend only on the covariance of the couplings. We also study fluctuations: at an interior minimizer, an explicit variance bound transfers the limiting law of a logarithmic linear statistic to the free energy. For Gaussian couplings, this yields Gaussian fluctuations. At a boundary minimizer, assuming a simple regular edge with GOE Tracy-Widom fluctuations and a one-edge reduction, we transfer the edge fluctuations to the free energy.

title: Quasinormal Modes Criticality across Black Hole Extremality
summary: We investigate the extremal solution branch to nonextremal branch transition in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg anti-de Sitter black holes, where the nonlinear electromagnetic parameter $λ$ governs the existence of the extremal branch solution. At fixed pressure and charge, extremal black hole only exist for $λ\leqλ_c$. For $λ>λ_c$, the lowest Hawking temperature keeps nonzero. Near this threshold, the lowest temperature follows a linear critical scaling, $T_{\min}\propto(λ-λ_c)^{α_T}$. We investigate the corresponding dynamical behavior by computing the quasinormal modes of a massless scalar perturbation along the lowest-temperature black hole branch. As the critical threshold is approached, two complex-frequency quasinormal modes branches collide on the imaginary axis and reorganize into distinct purely imaginary branches. Then the imaginary parts of these modes, together with higher overtones, reach zero at the critical threshold, described by $Γ_n\propto(λ-λ_c)^{α_n}$, with $α_n\simeqα_T$. The resulting zero-damped modes become increasingly localized near the event horizon, and their relative damping rates closely follow the overtone spacing predicted by the near-horizon AdS$_2$ spectrum. Our results show that the thermodynamic and dynamical critical behavior remain closely connected even when extremal black hole solutions cease to exist, providing further evidence for the relevance of near-extremal spectral behavior in this distinct critical regime.

title: Daemon sub Ponte: The Cost of a Second Black Hole (A Scholium on an ER=EPR Thought Experiment)
comment: This concerns a question that has haunted the author since 2014, repeatedly set aside in favor of more pressing projects. As the project queue has shown no sign of shortening, the author has finally decided to address it
summary: A thought experiment in the ER=EPR and related literature involves collecting the Hawking radiation of an old black hole, then collapsing it into a second, entangled black hole. In this short note, we examine the resources required by this idealized conversion. More specifically, we are interested in answering the question: how much external energy is needed to form the second black hole? Assuming a semiclassical bound on the information capacity of the newly formed black hole, we derive a conditional lower bound on external energy and a complementary constraint on correlations retained by the exterior degrees of freedom. We also distinguish entropy-level feasibility from the requirements for exact and approximate purification. We illustrate these requirements via a Page curve analysis.

title: Comment on "Zero temperature, degenerate fermion stars" [S. Boatto, M.B. Paranjape, V. Pessanha, C.A.D. Zarro. ArXiv: 2609.20950]
summary: In contrast to S. Boatto et al. \cite{Boat}, the degree of compactification or compactness is clarified for the self-gravitating spheric star of fermionic matter.

title: Leaving Quantum Bias on the Table: Pushforwards as a Path to Quantum Advantage in Constrained Optimization
summary: Constrained quantum samplers often produce infeasible outputs that retain information about good feasible solutions. We develop a post-measurement framework that constructs problem-dependent classical feasibility maps from constraint-violation statistics and pushes the raw quantum sampling law forward onto the feasible set. The probability of each repaired solution is the total raw mass of its repair preimage, enlarging the successful sampling event from a target feasible set to its full repair preimage.
